title: refactor(types): bind WidgetInput.type to the shared arm vocabulary, and record the two divergences left unrepaired
body:
Fixes #5675

One mechanical convergence, pinned. Two design divergences recorded and raised as questions, **not** changed — the card explicitly declined to pre-judge them, and the triage ruling on it narrowed the scope to exactly this split.

Verified at `f2d6a27d5` (the final commit; every result below was produced on that tree).

---

## 1. The member-equality measurement — done FIRST, because it decided whether this was mechanical at all

If `WidgetInput`'s eleven inline literals had differed from `ComponentInputControlType` in either direction, this would have been a behaviour question — silently widening or narrowing what a widget may declare — and would have been reported instead of implemented. Measured by parsing both declarations out of source rather than by eye:

```
WidgetInput.type     (11): string number boolean enum array object color date code file slot
ComponentInputControlType (11): string number boolean enum array object color date code file slot
ComponentInputControlTypeSchema, the enforced half (11): identical

SET  widget - base : []
SET  base - widget : []
MEMBER-EQUAL      : True
ORDER-SENSITIVE equal : True
```

Equal in both directions, and in the same order. So the change is a pure convergence: **no value a widget author may write changes.**

`type` stays the **single-kind** form. `ComponentInput.type` additionally accepts an *array* of arms for a union-typed key (#3832); importing that capability here would be a widening rather than a convergence, so it was deliberately left out — the same disposition #4972 recorded when it left this face alone. A test asserts the restraint, so granting it later is a decision someone makes rather than a line that drifts in.

## 2. What the convergence buys — one drift direction was silent

`WidgetRegistry.load()` in `@object-ui/core` translates each `WidgetInput` into a `ComponentInput` and passes `type` **straight through**:

```ts
inputs: manifest.inputs?.map((input) => ({
  name: input.name,
  type: input.type,
  ...
  enum: input.options,
```

That assignment is genuinely type-checked (`meta?: ComponentMeta`, `inputs?: ComponentInput[]`) — measured below, not assumed. Before this change it compiled only because two independently maintained lists happened to agree. And the two drift directions were **asymmetric**: an arm *removed* from the shared vocabulary breaks the assignment loudly, while an arm *added* to it produced no error anywhere — widget authoring would simply have stayed narrower than component registration, with nothing in the tree saying so. After this change neither direction is expressible.

## 3. The identity pin, and why the value assertions are not it

A TS type alias erases at runtime, so **a member-identical restatement is indistinguishable from the derived type by any assignability or runtime check** — the trap `spec-derived-unions.test.ts` records one file over. Every value assertion in the new suite passes just as green on the defect as on the fix. So the pin is **source-text**: `WidgetInput.type` is spelled exactly `ComponentInputControlType`, the name is imported from `./base.js`, no local alias of the vocabulary is declared, and no arm literal is written anywhere in the module's code (comments stripped first, so the scan reads code and not the doc block that discusses the vocabulary).

### The member-identical ablation — the contrast IS the evidence

Two legs, each mutated, **confirmed on disk by grepping the injected and the removed text** (never an editor exit code), each direction predicted before running, each restored by an `EXIT INT TERM` trap with `git diff HEAD --stat` verified empty afterwards.

| leg | mutation | vitest | `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json` |
|---|---|---|---|
| **A — adversarial** | a private `type WidgetInputControlType = <the same 11 members>` in `widget.ts`, `type:` pointed at it | **4 failed \| 8 passed** | **exit 0 — GREEN** |
| **B — real relapse** | the eleven literals inline again, i.e. exactly `origin/main`'s shape | **3 failed \| 9 passed** | **exit 0 — GREEN** |
| restored | — | 12 passed | exit 0 |

The four that fail in leg A are precisely the identity pins:

```
× is spelled exactly `ComponentInputControlType`
× imports that name from the module that declares it
× declares no local alias of the vocabulary
× writes no arm literal anywhere in the module code
```

Leg B fails three of those (it declares no alias, so that one correctly stays green). **Every value, seam and doc assertion stayed green in both legs, and `type-check` stayed green in both** — a member-identical restatement is completely invisible to `tsc`. That is the whole point: a value-only suite passes *on* the defect, and a type-only gauge cannot see it either.

No rebuild leg applies to these two: the suite reads `widget.ts` off disk with `readFileSync` and imports its siblings by relative source path, and `packages/types/tsconfig.test.json` sets `"paths": {}` so `tsc` resolves them relatively too. No `dist/` is anywhere in that resolution path. The mutations turning the pins red is itself the proof that the mutated source is what ran.

### Calibrating the seam gauge — the first attempt was a false green, and it is reported as one

To show the `WidgetRegistry` assignment is *really* type-checked, a probe arm (`ComponentInputControlType | 'OS5675_SEAM_PROBE'`) was added to `WidgetInput.type` and `@object-ui/core`'s `type-check` run. Predicted red.

**First run came back exit 0 — green.** Not because the seam is untyped, but because `@object-ui/core` resolves `@object-ui/types` through `dist/`, and `dist/` had not been rebuilt. That is the classic no-rebuild false green, and it is recorded here rather than quietly re-run: the initial reading was wrong, and the reason a reader should distrust it is the reason itself.

Re-run with the rebuild — mutation confirmed in source, then confirmed to have **reached `dist/widget.d.ts`** before the measurement was read:

```
dist: probe present (expect 1)     : 1
208:    type: ComponentInputControlType | 'OS5675_SEAM_PROBE';

core type-check exit: 2
src/registry/WidgetRegistry.ts(175,11): error TS2322: Type '{ name: string;
  type: ComponentInputControlType | "OS5675_SEAM_PROBE"; ... }[] | undefined'
  is not assignable to type 'ComponentInput[] | undefined'.
```

So the seam is live and the "loud direction" claim is measured, not asserted: widening `WidgetInput` by one arm is type-equivalent to the shared vocabulary losing an arm `WidgetInput` retains, which is exactly that direction. The silent direction follows from assignability — a narrower union is assignable to a wider one — and the pre-change tree was its standing demonstration.

**The restore leg rebuilt `dist/` too**, and is verified byte-exact against the pre-probe build (`f4d02d6c…`), so no probe survived into any later measurement.

## 4. Published surface — the emitted `.d.ts`, before and after

`WidgetInput` is published, so the surface change is shown rather than inferred.

```
dist/widget.d.ts   eb9beb7a…  ->  f4d02d6c…     CHANGED
dist/index.d.ts    02ad8ce7…  ->  02ad8ce7…     byte-identical
```

```diff
+import type { ComponentInputControlType } from './base.js';
 export interface WidgetInput {
     name: string;
-    /** Input field type */
-    type: 'string' | 'number' | 'boolean' | 'enum' | 'array' | 'object' | 'color' | 'date' | 'code' | 'file' | 'slot';
+    type: ComponentInputControlType;
```

**Gauge calibration:** the gauge registered a difference on this very change, and again on the seam probe, so it is demonstrably not a dead instrument. The `index.d.ts` byte-identical reading must **not** be read as "no published change" — it names `WidgetInput` as a re-export specifier but carries none of its shape, which is the same control #4972 recorded for `@object-ui/core`'s barrel. Exactly one emitted declaration changed.

---

## The two divergences this PR deliberately did NOT change — raised as questions

Both are now recorded in `WidgetInput`'s own doc block, so they stop living only in a closed card's body, and the doc block's load-bearing sentences are pinned (a doc block is the entire deliverable for this half, and nothing else would notice it being deleted).

### Q1. `options` here vs `enum` on `ComponentInput` — rename, or document the split?

One concept, two names, one package. It is **adapted, not broken**: `WidgetRegistry.load()` maps `enum: input.options` at the seam, and `sdui-parser`'s serializer reads `enum` downstream. So nothing fails to arrive; the cost is a hand-written rename every reader of both faces must know about, and that a future key added to either side can forget.

- **A — leave it, documented.** Zero risk; the cost stays.
- **B — rename `WidgetInput.options` to `enum`.** One vocabulary end to end, adapter line disappears. But it is a published key on a published type, and the in-repo importer count (zero besides the declaration and its re-export) says nothing about external consumers — the same unmeasurable half #5674 recorded.
- **C — rename `ComponentInput.enum` to `options`.** Strictly worse: far more consumers, and `enum` is what the published manifest already carries.

**Recommendation: A for this PR, B as a deprecate-then-delete card if the merge question is ever answered "yes".** B is right on naming and wrong on mandate — this card had none for a surface change, and a rename with no measured pull is exactly the scope bar the triage ruling applied.

### Q2. The five keys `ComponentInput` carries that this face does not — add, or leave?

`inputType`, `min`, `max`, `step`, `placeholder` (thirteen keys against eight; `options`/`enum` accounts for the other direction). They are not lost in translation — they are unwritable from a widget manifest to begin with.

Measured before leaving them out, and this is the part that changes the answer: **no reader in this repository consumes any of the five on `ComponentInput` either**, and `sdui-parser`'s serializer forwards six keys (`name`, `type`, `required`, `enum`, `binding`, `description`) and none of these. So adding them here would mirror surface that nothing reads on the face it already lives on.

**Recommendation: leave them out.** Adding inert keys to a second published face is the opposite of the convergence this card is about. The prior question is what to do about them on `ComponentInput`, which is a different surface and out of this card's fence — filed separately as #5905 for triage.

---

## Verification

Union run after the final commit, at `f2d6a27d5`. Heavy legs went through the shared verify lock; exit codes captured before any pipe.

```
vitest widget-input-control-vocabulary + WidgetRegistry   35 passed (2 files)
pnpm --filter @object-ui/types type-check                 exit 0
  > tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.examples.json && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json
pnpm --filter @object-ui/core  type-check                 exit 0
  > tsc --noEmit && tsc -p tsconfig.test.json
```

Gates, each quoting its own printed verdict line:

```
check-changeset-presence   exit 0  ✅ 2 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this
                                      change declares 1 changeset(s)
check-changeset-no-major   exit 0  ✅ No changeset declares a `major` bump.
check-changeset-fixed      exit 0  ✅ All workspace packages are in the changeset fixed group.
check-control-bytes        exit 0  ✅ OK (scanned 4910 tracked text file(s); skipped 85 binary)
check-spec-symbol-derivation exit 0 ✅ 1300 files scanned against 4959 spec export names
check-type-check-coverage  exit 0  ✅ test type-check coverage: 41/41 packages compile their tests
check-lint-coverage        exit 0  ✅ lint coverage: 46/46 packages linted
check-package-self-import  exit 0  ✅ No package names itself inside its own src/.
```

Two of these are reported with the coverage they actually have, not the coverage they look like they have:

- **`check-spec-symbol-derivation` is not evidence about this defect.** It guards spec-symbol collisions, and #5899 measured that it skips non-exported declarations. It was green on `origin/main` — i.e. green *on* the restatement — so citing it as coverage here would be citing a gate that never looked.
- **`check-doc-snippet-types` exited 1 and is reported as NOT RUN, not as failing.** Its own verdict line says why: `The snippet program was NOT run: the packages it resolves against are not built`. It needs a full-repo build; this worktree built only the packages under test. It reads no file this PR touches. CI builds the farm.

**Lint — a declared narrowing, with its three measurements.** Run scoped to the affected package rather than the repo:

1. **Population read from eslint's own config**, not from a guess about which files count: eslint resolved and linted **111 files** in `packages/types`.
2. **Count read from `--format json`**: 111 files, 0 errors under the invocation CI actually uses (`turbo run lint` → `eslint .`; `--no-inline-config` appears nowhere in CI). Both touched files are in the population, each `errors=0 warnings=0`.
3. **Invariance for untouched files**: `eslint.config.js` declares no type-aware program — `projectService`, `parserOptions.project` and `project:` are all absent (grep count 0) — so no file's lint verdict depends on another file's types, and editing `widget.ts` cannot move the verdict of any file that did not itself change.

With all three, the narrowing is a measurement rather than a skipped run. (For completeness: a stricter `--no-inline-config` pass surfaces 4 pre-existing `no-restricted-imports` errors in four files that carry sanctioned inline disables — none of them touched here, and not an invocation CI performs.)

## Scope

Touched: `packages/types/src/widget.ts`, one new test, one changeset. `ComponentInput` was not touched. `plugin-scope.ts` was not touched — #5674's stage-1 deprecation landed there and stage 2 is tracked by #5892; neither is addressed here.

⚠️ **One conflict between the dispatch and the fence, surfaced rather than silently resolved:** the dispatch asked for "a comment on both declarations naming the other", and also fenced `ComponentInput` as do-not-touch. The fence won — the divergence note lives on `WidgetInput` only, which is also what the triage ruling on the card specified. `ComponentInput` therefore still has no pointer back at this face; if a note there is wanted, it needs a separate change.

Left **draft** deliberately: this is a published-surface change and the two questions above want a PM answer before it moves.
